answer: New identities are capped at 6 per origin per day and each pays a 5 dollar alias fee, so 1000 clones must spread across 167 origins and prepay the whole bill before any can vote. Origin metadata enters the admission record, letting auditors group a ferrous of accounts arriving through one uplink. Slashed clusters forfeit their refundable bond, so marginal clone cost rises with cluster size instead of falling. Honest agents register once and never meet the relic, and one established agent still equals one vote, so rented glacier add weightless noise rather than leverage.
